newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGBs end higher, receive boost from BOJ comments.
newsitem.headline: JGBs end higher, receive boost from BOJ comments.

text.p: The key September 10-year Japanese government bond futures contract extended gains toward the close and ended higher after receiving a boost from comments by the Bank of Japan governor.

"Market players had probably been waiting to make sure (officials such as) the BOJ governor and the Economic Planning Agency minister didn't say anything out of the ordinary (at a bankers' convention). When they didn't, JGBs were bought," a trader for a European brokerage house said.
The trader said that although market players were cautious, positive technical charts were pushing JGBs upwards.
"Everyone is cautious, but there is no reason to sell JGBs right now," the trader for a European brokerage house said.
Market players are conscious of the fact that technical charts have turned positive, and this is boosting JGBs despite traders' wariness about the recent rises, he said.
The September ended at 124.73, up from Wednesday's close of 124.50. Turnover was 30,007 contracts.
The benchmark 182nd JGB yield stood at 2.295 percent as of 0636 GMT, down from Wednesday's close of 2.315 percent.
Some said firmness of cash bonds was the primary reason for the firmness of JGB futures on Thursday.
The benchmark 182nd cash JGB yield fell below 2.3 percent on Thursday for the first time since May 2.
Cash bonds, especially the 177th and 178th 10-year JGBs with a little less than eight years left to maturity, were firm. a trader for a trust bank's securities unit.
Cash bonds have not been sold too much in general, which is why JGB futures have been firm, he said.
But market players have generally been long this week, and a steep rise from current levels is unlikely unless fresh buy factors emerge, the trader said.
In another recent development, the liquidity of the 174th 10-year JGB, now considered the cheapest-to-deliver cash JGB for the September futures contract, has been tight, the first trader said.

"An agricultural financial institution has continuosly conducted target buying of the 174th since about March and April. It is unclear how much of the 174th they have actually been able to obtain... but the volume of their target buying trades was huge," he said.
Target buying of JGBs involves the selling of out-of-the-money JGB put options.

If JGBs fall and the put options come in the money, the seller obtains the desired JGB issue. If they expire without being executed, the option writer gets the premium from having sold the put option.

BOJ governor Yasuo Matsushita said in a speech at a bankers' convention on Thursday: "In managing our current monetary policy, it is appropriate to carefully watch developments (in the economy and prices), while continuing to put emphasis on strengthening the basis for economic recovery."
